quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it will make the problem worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull over as soon as safely possible. Avoid braking, as it can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Which riding formation keeps a group of riders closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space to stay safe. Use a single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: How can you tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the back of the bike.
The back end jerks from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk side to side. You usually won't hear a tire fail while riding.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection will usually take just a few minutes.

questions.question: If you are riding beside another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay beside the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is unsafe because you may be in the vehicle's blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if danger appears. Either speed up or drop back to move away from the vehicle.

questions.question: Which item provides the best face protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: The front brake of a motorcycle:

options.text: Provides less than half the stopping power.
Provides about 70 percent of the stopping power.
Should only be used on wet roads.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of the stopping power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much stronger than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider prevent other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: By making angry gestures at other drivers
By riding in the center of the lane
By riding in the left side of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves no large space on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share your lane.

questions.question: A group of riders should merge onto a highway in what formation?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works best during normal riding. However, use a single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze the front brake hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Get used to using both brakes every time you slow down or stop. If you need to stop quickly, use both brakes. This habit makes it easier to apply both brakes in an emergency.

questions.question: The gear shift lever is located:

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot. To shift to a higher gear, put your foot under the lever and lift. To downshift, push the lever down.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Not worry about space between riders.
Keep more space than usual between riders.
Keep half the normal space between riders.
Keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space around each rider for safety.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep safe distance around each rider.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signals before changing lanes.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others, signal your moves, keep safe distance, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready for changes in traffic.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.
In the middle of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right side of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of the lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A rectangular sign usually tells you:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black lettering give rules like speed limits. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Both the front and rear brakes.
Either the front or rear brake, not both.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Follow other vehicles more closely than usual.
Brake later than you would alone.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight. Your motorcycle will need more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing sooner, keep more distance behind other vehicles, and leave larger gaps when crossing or merging.

questions.question: If your rear tire skids, it:

options.text: Only matters if the front tire also skids.

questions.explanation: A rear tire skid is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. Once locked, you lose control of direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the:

options.text: Motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
Motorcycle may speed up too quickly.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Why is riding directly next to another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. They could move into your lane without warning. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding. The wobble will likely stop on its own.
Slowly release the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly release the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle to slow down. Lean your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Once safely off the road, find out what caused the wobble.

questions.question: Which of these should you NOT do to improve your safety when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when safe to do so.
Stay farther back from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: For safe night riding, you should slow down, use your high beam when no other vehicles are near, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you. Their headlights light up the road and their taillights show bumps in the road.

questions.question: Which one of these does NOT help reduce serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: To reduce injury risk, wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing. A windshield does not reduce serious injury.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider safely returns to the original lane before starting to pass. This pattern continues until all riders have safely passed.

questions.question: What best helps prevent head or neck injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A load placed too high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can upset the motorcycle's balance.

questions.question: When braking on a surface with low traction, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the rear brake.
Do not use the front brake.

questions.explanation: On a surface with low traction, use caution and apply the brakes more gently than usual.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, how should you position yourself?

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver already sees you.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. The center position is where the driver is most likely to notice you.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's total braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: You need more space to stop when the road is slippery. Increase your following distance if the pavement is wet, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up—it will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you safely can.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is located on the left handlebar of a motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent serious injury?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots that support your ankles, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not provide protection.

questions.question: When should you use both brakes to slow or stop?
questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the most stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do at a blind intersection with a stop sign?

options.text: Stop at the sign and then proceed through.
Ignore the sign to get a better look ahead.
Stop at the sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop where the sign indicates. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for approaching traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for at least one hour
After riding for more than 8 hours

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes occur on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes of starting to ride.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?

options.text: Slowing of body and brain functions

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing of body and brain functions
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down both physical and mental functions. It impairs your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Which material provides the best protection for motorcycle clothing?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcyclists. Wear clothing made of leather that covers your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: Which item is NOT considered protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Protective clothing includes sturdy jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves. A stocking cap is not protective gear.
